# Transaction REJECTION vectors:
#   <label> <verdict> <corpus-exception> <bound-violated> <txbytes>
# All hex is without 0x. `bound-violated` is `-` for a `decode` row.
#
# SOURCE: ethereum/execution-specs release tests@v20.0.1 (87aba1a38),
# asset fixtures.tar.gz, transaction_tests/. Each case pairs raw txbytes
# with the TransactionException the specification expects.
#
# THE VERDICT IS READ FROM THE BYTES, NOT FROM THE EXCEPTION NAME, and
# that distinction was forced by measurement rather than chosen. All
# sixteen cases the corpus names TYPE_4_INVALID_AUTHORITY_SIGNATURE in
# fact carry a field wider than EIP-7702's own assert -- an `r` or `s` of
# 33 bytes, or a `y_parity` of 2 -- and ALL SIXTEEN are additionally
# labelled S_TOO_HIGH, which reads as a malleability rule and is here a
# width violation. Classifying by name put every one on the wrong side.
#
# NOTE THE CORPUS SPELLS THAT LABEL AS ONE COMPOUND STRING:
# `TYPE_4_INVALID_AUTHORITY_SIGNATURE|TYPE_4_INVALID_AUTHORITY_SIGNATURE_S_TOO_HIGH`,
# and carries no bare TYPE_4_INVALID_AUTHORITY_SIGNATURE anywhere. The
# corpus-exception column below records the truncated form, so grepping
# the corpus for this file's own value finds nothing -- match on the
# prefix, or on the compound string above.
#
#   reject  some field exceeds a width a specification states, so it is
#           decidable from the bytes and this layer must refuse it.
#
#   decode  every field is within bounds. What is wrong needs a recovered
#           authority or a fork rule, which this layer does not own, so
#           these MUST decode here and be refused above.
#
# Refusing a `decode` row would make this client reject transactions the
# network accepts; accepting a `reject` row would let malformed bytes
# through. Both are defects, which is why both directions are tested.
#
# The classifier is an independent RLP reader applied to the published
# octets -- it never asks the implementation under test what it thinks,
# which would make these rows agree with the code by construction.
#
# Rows: 122 reject, 2 decode. Dropped by a 640-byte cap: 0.
#
# How each corpus exception class actually partitions:
#   NONCE_OVERFLOW: reject=14
#   TYPE_4_EMPTY_AUTHORIZATION_LIST: decode=2
#   TYPE_4_INVALID_AUTHORITY_SIGNATURE: reject=16
#   TYPE_4_INVALID_AUTHORIZATION_FORMAT: reject=92
